concept.name: Senkou Span A
concept.definition: The faster cloud boundary: the average of Tenkan-sen and Kijun-sen, plotted 26 periods ahead of the current bar, forming the top of the Kumo (cloud) when above Senkou Span B and the bottom when below it.
concept.intuition: It averages the short and medium equilibria and projects them forward, marking the near edge of expected future support or resistance.
concept.mechanics: Senkou Span A = (Tenkan-sen + Kijun-sen)/2, shifted 26 bars forward. The cloud is bullish (green) when Span A is above Span B and bearish (red) when below; an A-B cross changes cloud color, an ebb-and-flow trend signal.
concept.formula: Senkou Span A = (Tenkan-sen + Kijun-sen) / 2, plotted 26 periods into the future.
concept.failure_modes: The forward shift is a display convention, not foresight - the value is fully determined by past data; cloud signals whipsaw when the market has no trend.
concept.misconceptions: 'Plotted in the future' does not mean it predicts future support - it is today's midpoint average drawn ahead of the current bar.
concept.example: Tenkan 104 and Kijun 103 give Senkou Span A = 103.5, shown 26 bars ahead of today.
